nodes.question: What type of methodology was applied in the assessment focused on residue management at the farm?
nodes.answer: The assessment applied consequential life cycle assessment (LCA) methodology.
nodes.paragraph: This was compared to the mono-digestion of cattle manure and a baseline sce- nario of soil incorporation of residues, using agricul- tural modelling and consequential LCA. Methods Goal and scope Definition of the system An example-farm of 1,0 hectares and 560 dairy cat- tle was modelled, under Danish conditions. The num- ber of cattle was decided based on the amount of feed that could be produced at 1,0 hectares (detailed data included in the Supplementary information (SI)). The assessment was focused on the management of residues at the farm, including the cattle manure and the cover crop- and straw residues, applying conse- quential LCA methodology (Brand o et al. 2022). The farm area was divided into two crop rotation systems of 500 hectares each (rotation 1 and 2), of which one was included in the LCA (Fig. 1). These 500 hectares were used for cultivation of spring bar - ley, with under-sown cover crops (rotation 1).

nodes.question: What is Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) and its purpose?
nodes.answer: Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) is an internationally standardized method used to quantify the potential environmental impacts of products by considering their full life cycle.
nodes.paragraph: 2018). Life cycle assessment (LCA) is an internationally standardised method to quantify the potential environmental impacts of products by taking into consideration the full life cycle of the product (ISO 14040, 2006). Several literature reviews have been conducted in the field of LCA of electronic products (Ghisellini et al. 2023; Andrae 2016; Teixeira et al. 2020; Nunes et al. 2021; Sub- ramanian and Yung 2016; He et al. 2023). Most of these reviews focus on consumer electronics. Some reviews have been conducted in specific areas of healthcare, such as environmental sustainability of mobile health technolo- gies (Dekimpe et al. 2022), comparison of single-use and reusable healthcare devices and products (Keil et al. 2022; S rensen et al. 2022), pharma-LCAs (Yang et al. 2020; De Soete et al. 2014), and environmental sustainability of surgi - cal procedures (Papadopoulou et al. 2022). However, to our knowledge, there is no review focused on EHDs yet. Also, LCA studies of EHDs used to conduct surgery (electronic surgical devices) are rarely addressed in the literature.

nodes.question: What are the four main steps of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA)?
nodes.answer: The four main steps of LCA are goal and scope definition, Life Cycle Inventory (LCI), Life Cycle Impact Assessment (LCIA), and interpretation of results.

Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) is among the most widely adopted methodologies for quantifying the environmen- tal impacts of products or services throughout their entire lifecycle, providing a robust basis for environmental sus- tainability assessments and circular economy strategies (Hellweg and Mil i Canals 2014; ISO 2020a; Lei et al. 2021; Br ndstr m and Saidani 2022; Sica et al. 2022). LCA consists of four main steps, namely, goal and scope definition, Life Cycle Inventory (LCI), Life Cycle Impact Assessment (LCIA), and interpretation of results (ISO 2020a; ISO 2020b). nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What is the main purpose of Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) according to the paragraph?
nodes.answer: The main purpose of LCA is to provide a standardized methodology that guarantees rigour and uniformity in calculating environmental impacts, supporting the evaluation of alternative production pathways, and aiding in informed decision-making processes within the circular economy.
nodes.paragraph: 2019; Beylot et al. 2020; Schulz et al. 2020). As LCA is a standardised methodology, it guarantees rigour and uniformity in the calculations of environmental impacts, helping comparability of results and transparency in evaluation processes (Hellweg and Mil i Canals 2014). By delivering comprehensive quantitative insights, LCA supports the evaluation of alternative production pathways, fostering transitions from linear to circular systems and assessing the potential consequences of adopting alterna- tive productions (Prado et al. 2017; Br ndstr m and Saidani 2022; Sica et al. 2022). While a product may exhibit high circularity performance, this does not necessarily lead to a reduction in environmental impacts (Pe a et al. 2021; Roos Lindgreen et al. 2021). Therefore, LCA provides a scientific and methodological basis for measuring the environmental performance of products and processes within the circular economy, supporting more informed decision-making pro- cesses (Serenella et al. 2015; Byrne et al. 2017; Cordella et al. 2020). nodes.answer: LCA assesses systems "cradle-to-grave," from gathering materials from the earth to returning materials to the earth.
